# Lab 2.8: Time Travel, Fail-safe & Undelete

## What We Are Going to Do
Query a table as it was a few minutes ago, restore deleted rows and a dropped table, undelete a dataset, and set the time travel window.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Delete some rows, then read the past.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">DELETE FROM lab02.trips_clone WHERE start_station_name LIKE '%Capitol%';

SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_5_min_ago
FROM lab02.trips_clone
FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 5 MINUTE);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Restore the deleted rows.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">INSERT INTO lab02.trips_clone
SELECT * FROM lab02.trips_clone
  FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 5 MINUTE)
WHERE start_station_name LIKE '%Capitol%';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[CLI] Restore a dropped table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">TS=$(date -d '-2 minutes' +%s%3N)
bq rm -f -t lab02.trips_restored
bq cp lab02.trips_restored@$TS lab02.trips_restored
bq show lab02.trips_restored</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The `@` value is a time in milliseconds before the table was deleted.

4. **[SQL] Undelete a dataset.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE SCHEMA lab02_tmp OPTIONS (location = 'US');
CREATE TABLE lab02_tmp.t AS SELECT 1 AS x;
DROP SCHEMA lab02_tmp CASCADE;
UNDROP SCHEMA lab02_tmp;
SELECT * FROM lab02_tmp.t;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[Console] Set the time travel window.** Open `lab02 → Edit details → Advanced options → Time travel window`. Set it to **2 days**. A shorter window lowers physical storage cost.

6. **[CLI] Same setting from the CLI.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq update --max_time_travel_hours=48 lab02</span>
</code></pre>

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Time travel | Read any point in the last 2–7 days |
| Dropped table | Restored with `bq cp table@time` |
| Dropped dataset | Restored with `UNDROP SCHEMA` |
| Fail-safe | 7 more days, recovery only through Google support |
